ALMANAC.arena.Description: On Mars, dust was choking off power to the InSight lander. The solution was to drop sand onto a panel. The wind carried larger grains across it and swept the fine dust away.
ALMANAC.arena.Title: Cleaning with sand
ALMANAC.buzon.Description: The spare filters were square and the opening was round. Following instructions over the radio, astronauts built an adapter from bags, cardboard, duct tape, and a hose.
ALMANAC.buzon.Title: The Apollo 13 mailbox
ALMANAC.co2.Description: The danger comes from the carbon dioxide (CO₂) you breathe out building up around you. It can make you clumsy and sleepy before it causes more serious harm.
ALMANAC.co2.Title: The air you breathe out
ALMANAC.ejercicio.Description: Space station astronauts do about two hours of exercise a day on a treadmill, a bike, and a resistance machine. In the game you run outside. Real astronauts work out inside the spacecraft.
ALMANAC.ejercicio.Title: Gym in space
ALMANAC.fuga.Description: The cabin hull has lost its seal. Each open hole reduces the oxygen available in the minigame.
ALMANAC.fuga.Title: We have a leak!
ALMANAC.fulguracion.Description: A giant flash of light and X-rays from the Sun. It takes about 8 minutes to reach us. Flares are classified by the letters B, C, M, and X. Each class is about 10 times stronger than the one before it.
ALMANAC.fulguracion.Title: Solar flare
ALMANAC.huesos.Description: Without Earth's gravity, bones and muscles do less work and become smaller and weaker. Daily exercise is the best defense.
ALMANAC.huesos.Title: Bones in space
ALMANAC.Intro: As things happen on the mission, you'll unlock cards that explain the science behind them.
ALMANAC.Label: Almanac
ALMANAC.LockedText: Unlocks when you encounter this on the mission.
ALMANAC.micrometeorito.Description: Tiny pieces of rock or metal, sometimes smaller than a grain of sand, travel at tens of kilometers per second. At that speed they can puncture a hull, so spacecraft use layers of shielding.
ALMANAC.micrometeorito.Title: Micrometeoroids
ALMANAC.parche.Description: Press and hold a patch to set it in place. If you let go too soon, the leak opens again.
ALMANAC.parche.Title: Emergency repair
ALMANAC.particulas.Description: Sometimes after a strong flare, the Sun sends out fast-moving particles that can harm astronauts. No one knows for sure whether they will arrive. That's why crews move to the best-shielded area when an alert goes out.
ALMANAC.particulas.Source: NASA — space radiation and solar energetic particles (SEP)
ALMANAC.particulas.Title: Solar particle storm
ALMANAC.polvo.Description: Lunar dust is like ground glass. With no wind or water on the Moon, the grains keep their sharp edges. Static electricity makes the dust cling, so it comes back when you wipe it off.
ALMANAC.polvo.Title: Lunar dust
ALMANAC.soyuz.Description: In 2018, the space station lost air through a 2 mm hole in a Soyuz spacecraft. The crew covered it with tape and later sealed it with gauze and epoxy.
ALMANAC.soyuz.Title: The hole in Soyuz
ALMANAC.temblores.Description: Apollo astronauts left seismometers on the Moon. Between 1969 and 1977, they recorded 28 shallow moonquakes, roughly magnitude 2 to 5.
ALMANAC.temblores.Source: NASA — Shrinking Moon May Be Generating Moonquakes (2019)
ALMANAC.temblores.Title: Moonquakes
ALMANAC.tierra-fija.Description: The Moon always shows Earth the same face. From the Moon, Earth stays in nearly the same spot in the sky. An antenna aimed correctly stays connected. The signal takes about 1.3 seconds to reach Earth.
ALMANAC.tierra-fija.Title: Earth stays in place
ALMANAC.Title: What you've discovered
ALMANAC.tomates.Description: Veggie's Red Robin tomatoes were harvested several times. Scientists studied how the color of the light changes how much they grow and how they taste.
ALMANAC.tomates.Source: NASA NTRS — VEG-05 Tomato Crop Testing (2024)
ALMANAC.tomates.Title: Space tomatoes
ALMANAC.veggie.Description: Veggie is a suitcase-sized greenhouse on the space station. It uses LED lights in place of sunlight. Astronauts have grown lettuce, flowers, and tomatoes in it.
ALMANAC.veggie.Title: A space garden
ANTENNA.Note.apuntando: Press and hold to turn the antenna. Release when it points at Earth.
ANTENNA.Note.enviando: Message in transit… light takes {{seconds}} seconds to reach Earth.
APP.Rotate: Turn your phone upright to play.
APP.Title: Sol 7 Outpost
BASE.StormBlocked: The shelter protected the crew from the particle storm.
BASE.StormHit: A particle storm hit the crew.
DUST.SandStill: With no wind, the sand just sits there.
DUST.SandWind: That's it! The wind carries the sand and knocks the dust loose.
DUST.Scrub: Scrub the panel with your finger.
ENDING.Decisions: No one could have known that in advance. That's why, with every alert, astronauts have to make the same kind of decision you did.
ENDING.ganaste.Text: You kept the crew safe and completed the experiments. That's what putting your energy to good use looks like.
ENDING.ganaste.Title: Mission accomplished!
ENDING.RealWeather: The flares in this game really happened between October 3 and 10, 2026. The strongest was an M6.7 flare. That week, NASA recorded {{observed}}.
ENDING.Remo: Remo, the outpost manager. Crew: {{crew}} of {{max}}
ENDING.SimulatedMany: In your playthrough, {{count}} storms arrived because the game rolls the dice.
ENDING.SimulatedOne: In your playthrough, {{count}} storm arrived because the game rolls the dice.
ENDING.sin-ciencia.Text: The crew came home safely, but some experiments were left unfinished. Protecting against every risk comes at a cost. The mission was there to do science.
ENDING.sin-ciencia.Title: Everyone's safe, but the science is unfinished
ENDING.sin-tripulacion.Text: The crew couldn't carry on. In space, people come first. Without a crew, there is no mission.
ENDING.sin-tripulacion.Title: The outpost had to evacuate
EXPERIMENT.GoalMet: You've met the science goal! Now keep the crew safe until the mission ends.
EXPERIMENT.ProgressMany: You've completed {{science}} of {{goal}}. {{missing}} experiments remain to meet the mission goal.
EXPERIMENT.ProgressOne: You've completed {{science}} of {{goal}}. One experiment remains to meet the mission goal.
FILTER.Note.Choose: Tap the part BIP asks for.
FILTER.Note.Hold: Don't let go until it's sealed.
FILTER.Note.Wrong: Negative. That doesn't go there. The air is getting worse.
FILTER.Seal: Press and hold to secure the tape
HARVEST.Note.Ready: Wait for the tomatoes to turn red.
HARVEST.Note.seca: That plant had already dried out.
HARVEST.Note.temprano: It wasn't ready yet! The plant had to be replanted.

INTRO.Energy: Everything costs {{emphasis}}, and there's never enough for everything.
INTRO.Speaker: BIP · outpost computer
INTRO.Systems: There are {{emphasis}}: power, life support, food, and communications. Each day, the crew can service just one.
INTRO.Weather: Each sol, you'll see that day's {{emphasis}} if the antenna has a signal.
INTRO.Welcome: Captain, welcome to Sol 7 Outpost on the Moon. Our mission lasts {{sols}} sols.

LEAK.OpenHole: Hole {{number}}, press and hold to seal it
LEAK.Title: Stop the air from escaping!
PATCH.Hint: Tap a patch to rotate it 90°. It seals when the shape matches the hole.
PATCH.OpenHole: Hole {{number}}, the patch doesn't fit. Tap to rotate it.
PREP.ExperimentDetail: Advance the mission. You've completed {{science}} of {{goal}} experiments.
PREP.Save: Unspent energy carries over to tomorrow.
PREP.ShieldAlert: The crew heads to the shelter, where they'll be safe if a storm arrives.
PREP.ShieldQuiet: There's no alert today, so this would use extra energy.
PREP.ShieldUnknown: With no forecast, shielding is the safer choice, but it costs energy.
PREP.Title: How should we spend our energy today?
RESULT.AirDamage: There wasn't enough energy to produce oxygen. The crew loses 1 heart.
RESULT.ForecastLost: The antenna has no signal, so tomorrow's space weather forecast won't arrive from Earth.
RESULT.Hunger: The food ran out. The crew went hungry and loses 1 heart.
RESULT.Missed: You took a chance and the particle storm didn't arrive. This time, you got lucky.
RESULT.MissedShield: The particle storm didn't arrive. The shielding wasn't needed this time, but no one could have known that in advance.
RESULT.Quiet: The Sun was quiet. Nothing happened.
RESULT.QuietShield: The Sun was quiet. The shielding used energy and wasn't needed.
RESULT.Recharge: The panels are dusty and generated {{recharge}} of {{total}} energy today.
RESULT.Shielded: A particle storm arrived! The shielding protected the entire crew.
RESULT.StormHitMany: An unshielded particle storm hit the base! The crew loses {{count}} hearts.
RESULT.StormHitOne: An unshielded particle storm hit the base! The crew loses {{count}} heart.
RESULT.Wear: After {{limit}} sols without maintenance, the air got stuffy. The crew loses 1 heart.

ROUTINE.DustCost: The panels stay dirty after {{days}} of dust buildup and generate less energy.
ROUTINE.EmptyPantry: The pantry is empty! If no one harvests, the crew loses 1 heart.
ROUTINE.ExerciseGain: Keep the crew's bones and muscles strong. If you fail, the crew loses 1 heart.
ROUTINE.HarvestGain: Restock the pantry: +{{success}} rations (+{{failure}} if you fall short).
ROUTINE.NoForecast: The antenna still has no signal, so tomorrow's space weather forecast won't arrive.
ROUTINE.PanelGain: Clean panels generate more energy each sol.
ROUTINE.SkipHarvestMany: No one harvests today. The pantry will have {{count}} rations left.
ROUTINE.SkipHarvestOne: No one harvests today. The pantry will have {{count}} ration left.
ROUTINE.SkipPanels: The panels go uncleaned and start to collect dust.
ROUTINE.SupportGain: Keep the crew's air safe. If you fail, the crew loses 1 heart.
ROUTINE.Title: Captain, there are two tasks and the crew only has time for one. Protocol says it's your call.
ROUTINE.WearCost: Life support has gone {{days}} without maintenance. Skip it again today and the crew loses 1 heart.
RUN.Canvas: The astronaut runs across the Moon. There are craters on the ground and meteorites overhead.
RUN.Hint: Jump over craters. When a meteorite comes, {{emphasis}} so it passes overhead.
SETTINGS.Title: Volume and language
SHIP.antena.Detail: A moonquake shifted the antenna. Without a signal, tomorrow's space weather forecast from Earth won't arrive.
SHIP.antena.Fact: Earth barely moves in the lunar sky because the Moon always shows Earth the same face. Moonquakes do happen: seismometers left by the Apollo missions recorded 28 shallow quakes between 1969 and 1977.
SHIP.antena.Instructions: Press and hold to rotate the antenna. Release when it points at Earth. The message goes out when the signal turns green. Send 3 messages before time runs out.
SHIP.antena.LoseText: Only {{count}} of 3 messages went through. The outpost is out of contact for now.
SHIP.antena.Title: Aim at Earth!
SHIP.antena.WinText: Earth received the messages. Tomorrow's space weather forecast will arrive.
SHIP.cosecha.Detail: The tomatoes are ripening. If no one harvests them in time, they dry out.
SHIP.cosecha.Fact: Between December 2022 and March 2023, astronauts aboard the International Space Station grew dwarf Red Robin cherry tomatoes in Veggie, a small greenhouse with LED lights. They had already grown lettuce and even flowers.
SHIP.cosecha.Instructions: Tap each plant when it has red tomatoes. Tap too early and you uproot it. Wait too long and it dries out. Harvest 8 plants before time runs out.
SHIP.cosecha.LoseText: Only {{count}} plants were harvested. The crew will have to eat packaged food again.
SHIP.cosecha.Title: Harvest in time!
SHIP.cosecha.WinText: The crew will have fresh tomatoes alongside their packaged food.
SHIP.ejercicio.Detail: Without exercise, bones and muscles weaken. The panels go uncleaned.
SHIP.ejercicio.Fact: Astronauts on the International Space Station exercise about two hours a day on average. Without Earth's gravity, bones and muscles weaken and shrink. In real life, the crew exercises inside the spacecraft.
SHIP.ejercicio.Instructions: Tap the screen to jump over craters. Stay on the ground when a meteorite flies by. On the Moon you weigh about one sixth as much, so jumps are high and slow. Last 20 seconds with fewer than 3 stumbles.
SHIP.ejercicio.LoseText: The run ended at {{count}} meters. Without exercise, the crew gets weaker.
SHIP.ejercicio.Title: Time to run!
SHIP.ejercicio.WinText: The crew finished today's workout and kept their bones and muscles strong.
SHIP.filtro.Detail: The filter has been running too long. The panels stay dusty for another day.
SHIP.filtro.Fact: On Apollo 13, three astronauts built this kind of adapter with bags, cardboard, duct tape, and a hose, following instructions over the radio. They called it the mailbox.
SHIP.filtro.Instructions: The spare filter is square and the opening is round. Follow BIP's instructions before the air gets too stuffy.
SHIP.filtro.LoseText: The crew got dizzy before finishing. The panels are still dusty.
SHIP.filtro.Title: Build the adapter!
SHIP.filtro.WinText: The square filter now cleans the air through the round opening. The panels are still dusty.
SHIP.fugas.Detail: The hull has been punctured. Patch the holes before you run out of oxygen.
SHIP.fugas.Fact: In this simulation, covering a leak stops air from escaping while the patch sets.
SHIP.fugas.Instructions: Press and hold each hole to attach a patch. If you let go too soon, air escapes again. Seal all 9 before you run out of oxygen. With a mouse, patch one at a time. On a phone, you can use several fingers.
SHIP.fugas.LoseText: BIP closed the cabin to protect the rest of the ship. Repair the hull before going back in.
SHIP.fugas.Title: The ship is losing air!
SHIP.fugas.WinText: All the patches are holding. The crew can breathe easily again.
SHIP.parches.Detail: Micrometeoroids punctured the hull. Each hole has a different shape. Turn each patch until it fits.
SHIP.parches.Fact: In August 2018, the International Space Station began leaking air through a roughly 2 mm hole in the Soyuz MS-09 spacecraft. The crew covered it with tape and later sealed it with gauze soaked in epoxy. A micrometeoroid was suspected at first, but the hole had been made on Earth before launch.
SHIP.parches.Instructions: Tap each patch to rotate it 90°. When it matches the shape of the hole, it seals. Air keeps escaping until it fits. Seal all 8 before you run out of oxygen.
SHIP.parches.LoseText: BIP closed the cabin with {{percent}}% oxygen left. The hull needs more patching.
SHIP.parches.Title: Fit the patches!
SHIP.parches.WinText: Every patch is in place and oxygen has stopped escaping.
SHIP.polvo.Detail: Dust covers the panels and they produce less power. The air filter goes unchecked.
SHIP.polvo.Fact: In 2021, NASA cleaned a solar panel on its InSight lander on Mars by dropping sand on it. The wind swept the larger grains across the panel, knocking loose the fine dust.
SHIP.polvo.Instructions: Scrub with your finger. Watch out, the dust sticks again. There's another way…
SHIP.polvo.LoseText: The panel is only {{percent}}% clean. The air filter still needs changing.
SHIP.polvo.Title: Clean the solar panel!
SHIP.polvo.WinText: The panels are generating power again. The air filter went another day without being changed.
WEATHER.Credit: Real space weather · NASA DONKI · Oct 3–10, 2026 · archived data
WEATHER.FlareDetail: The Sun released a class {{letter}} flare ({{strength}}). Each class, from B to C to M to X, is about 10 times stronger than the last.
WEATHER.HiddenWarning: The antenna has gone unchecked for days, and today's forecast never arrived. A solar flare could still happen. You'll have to decide without a forecast.
WEATHER.KpDetail: Geomagnetic storm on Earth: {{index}} (the scale goes from 0 to 9).
WEATHER.PlasmaDetail: A plasma cloud left the Sun at {{speed}}. At that speed, it would take about {{travel}} to travel from the Sun to the Moon.
WEATHER.Regolith: Lunar soil, called regolith, helps block radiation. That's why the base is underground and the shelter is its most protected room.
WEATHER.Scale: Solar flare scale: today's flare was class {{flare}}. Each class is 10 times stronger than the last.
WEATHER.ScaleEmpty: Solar flare scale: no flares today.
WEATHER.Warning: A particle storm {{might}} follow a flare like this. No one knows whether it will.
